title: Wedding gifts have gotten complicated, and guests are confused
titleZh: 婚礼礼金送多少才合适
summary:
今年1月，29岁的布鲁克·鲍曼·布恩迎来了她梦寐以求的婚礼。她手捧缤纷的花束，沿着红毯款款走向新郎，晚宴上，宾客们在璀璨的迪斯科球灯下载歌载舞，直到天明。时至今日，仍有人对她说，那是他们参加过最令人难忘的婚礼之一。

来源：商业内幕；作者：Amanda Krause；原文发布时间：2025-08-15 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: When Brooke Bowman Boone, 29, got married in January, it was the day of her dreams. She carried a vibrant bouquet down the aisle toward her new husband, and her guests danced under disco balls all night. People still tell her it was one of the most fun weddings they'd ever attended.
paragraphs.contentZh: 今年1月，29岁的布鲁克·鲍曼·布恩迎来了她梦寐以求的婚礼。她手捧缤纷的花束，沿着红毯款款走向新郎，晚宴上，宾客们在璀璨的迪斯科球灯下载歌载舞，直到天明。时至今日，仍有人对她说，那是他们参加过最令人难忘的婚礼之一。

paragraphs.contentEn: Months later, though, one thing still surprises the North Carolina native: 27 people — nearly 20% of her guest list — didn't bring a gift to celebrate her big day. "It was shocking," she said. "We couldn't even receive a card? That would have been nice. It just felt like a slap in the face." For better or worse, she's not the only bride facing a modern problem: giving and receiving wedding gifts has gotten complicated.
paragraphs.contentZh: 不过，即便婚礼已过去数月，这位来自北卡罗来纳州的新娘仍有一件事难以释怀：婚礼宾客中，有27人——约占总人数的五分之一——没有带任何礼物来庆祝她的新婚之喜。她说：“实在难以置信。哪怕只是送张贺卡也好啊？至少会让我觉得自己被重视。但现在，我只觉得像是被无情地冷落了。”不管怎么说，她并不是唯一遇到这种现代难题的新娘：如今，结婚礼物的赠与与接受，已经变得越来越复杂。

paragraphs.contentEn: Naturally, my colleagues and I were grumbling about a busy wedding season when we landed on the topic of gifts. While some of us were shelling out $300 cash alongside registry presents, others opted for $100 bills tucked into cards. We were, to say the least, concerned. Were some of us spending too little? Were others giving over-the-top gifts? At least we gave gifts, right?
paragraphs.contentZh: 和同事们闲聊时，话题很自然就从吐槽婚礼扎堆转到了送礼这件事上。我们之中，有人在按照礼单送出礼物的同时，又额外塞了300美元现金；也有人只是在贺卡里夹了100美元。说实话，我们都有些纠结。是不是有人出手太寒酸？还是说有的人出手太阔绰？不过，至少我们都送了礼，总比空手强吧？

paragraphs.contentEn: A quick social-media search showed we're not alone in our confusion. On TikTok, people have questioned if there's an average or "normal" amount of cash everyone should gift at weddings these days. Others on Reddit have asked where registry items enter the equation. Unfortunately, there's no clear winning answer among average internet users. Some commenters say $50 cash is sufficient, while others say your gift — whether in the form of money or a present — should cost no less than $500.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在社交媒体上随便一搜，就会发现为此困扰的并不止我们。TikTok上，有人提问，现在参加婚礼，礼金是否存在一个“平均数”或者“公认的标准”？Reddit上，也有网友热议，如果新人列出了礼物清单，那现金礼金该怎么算。可惜的是，网友的讨论并没有得出一个明确、公认的答案。有人认为50美元就足够了；也有人坚持，不管是现金还是实物，其价值都不应低于500美元。

paragraphs.contentEn: Chelsea Fagan, the founder of The Financial Diet and author of "Having People Over," told Business Insider that the uncertainty partially stems from the modern "inflation of the entire wedding process." Whereas the average wedding was once small, local, and contained to a single day, it's now bigger, more luxurious, and comprised of multiple events, from multiday bachelor trips to welcome parties. "We're really opening our pockets to an unsustainable degree for weddings," the finance and etiquette writer said.
paragraphs.contentZh: The Financial Diet网站的创办者、《待客之道》一书作者切尔西·费根在接受《商业内幕》采访时指出，人们之所以如此纠结，部分原因在于“婚礼规格的水涨船高”。过去的婚礼规模较小，通常在当地举行，且一天之内就能完成；而如今，婚礼变得越发盛大奢华，往往包含多个环节，从持续数天的单身派对到迎宾晚宴。这位专注于财经与礼仪的作家认为：“现在人们在婚礼上的花费，已经达到了难以承受的程度。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In April, Credit Karma surveyed 1,106 American Gen Zers and millennials and found that 38% took on debt to attend weddings in the past year. BI has also reported that some people have spent over $10,000 to attend multiple ceremonies and receptions in less than three years. Gifts are only a small part of that equation, but they're expensive nonetheless. In an email to BI, Lauren Kay, the executive editor of The Knot, said a 2025 study from the publication shows that the average wedding guest spends $150 on a gift.
paragraphs.contentZh: 今年4月，Credit Karma公司针对1106名美国Z世代和千禧一代展开的调查显示，过去一年中，有38%的受访者为参加婚礼而背上债务。《商业内幕》早前的报道也指出，有些人在不到三年的时间里，为出席多场婚礼及相关宴会，累计支出已超过1万美元。礼物虽然只占总支出的一小部分，但同样不便宜。The Knot网站执行主编劳伦·凯在发给《商业内幕》的一封邮件中表示，该机构2025年的研究显示，婚礼宾客在礼物上的人均支出达到了150美元。

paragraphs.contentEn: Bowman Boone and her husband lived together for more than two years before getting married, so they didn't need to put an extensive registry together. Instead, they asked guests to contribute to a honeymoon fund. While the couple was thrilled to receive many cash and online deposits, Bowman Boone said their guests' efforts mattered most. "We did have people [in different financial situations], and I didn't look at any of them differently if they didn't give us a financial or physical gift," she told BI. "At the end of the day, everyone coming to my wedding was a gift in itself," she added. "I wanted everyone we invited to be there and celebrate us."
paragraphs.contentZh: 鲍曼·布恩与丈夫在结婚前已经同居了两年多，因此并不需要准备详细的礼物清单。他们只是希望宾客能为他们的“蜜月基金”出一份力。鲍曼·布恩坦言，虽然收到的不少现金和线上转账让她和丈夫非常欣喜，但她更看重的其实是宾客的心意。她告诉《商业内幕》：“宾客的经济条件各不相同，即便有人没有送礼金或实物礼物，我也不会对他们另眼相看。”她补充道：“归根结底，能来参加我婚礼的每一位宾客，本身就是一份礼物。我真心希望所有受邀的人都能到场，与我们一同庆祝。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Still, it stung when some family members and guests arrived without cards. Bowman Boone said it felt like her efforts as a host hadn't been reciprocated, and she couldn't understand why. Brides on social media have expressed similar disappointments after their weddings. "When we had 120 people at our wedding and we only received 12 cards and four gifts," one TikToker said in a recent viral video.
paragraphs.contentZh: 话虽如此，当部分亲友和宾客出席婚礼时连贺卡都没带，她的心里还是会觉得不是滋味。鲍曼·布恩表示，这让她觉得自己作为东道主的用心款待没有得到回应，而且她也无法理解原因。社交媒体上，不少新娘在婚礼后也表达了类似的失望。一位TikTok博主在最近一条爆火的视频中提到：“120位宾客的婚礼，最终只收到了12张贺卡和4份礼物。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Lauren Ladouceur attends weddings for a living. She's a leader in destination-wedding content creation, which involves attending weddings all over the world to capture high-quality iPhone content that couples can post on their social media pages. She told BI that no matter why some guests choose not to give gifts, it can still bother brides and grooms — sometimes even before their wedding day.
paragraphs.contentZh: 劳伦·拉杜瑟的职业就是参加婚礼。作为旅拍婚礼内容创作领域的头部博主，她的工作就是飞往世界各地，用iPhone拍摄高质量影像，供新人发布在社交媒体上。她在接受《商业内幕》采访时表示，无论宾客出于何种原因选择不送礼物，都可能让新人感到不快——有时这种情绪甚至在婚礼前就已萌生。

paragraphs.contentEn: "I've had couples come to me and say, 'How do I get people to donate to my honeymoon fund? How do I get people to buy from my registry? Nothing's coming in,'" Ladouceur said. "As we've moved away from tradition, which I ultimately think is a good thing, that transactional side to weddings is an unintended consequence."
paragraphs.contentZh: 拉杜瑟提到：“曾有新人来问我，‘怎样才能让宾客为我们的蜜月基金出点力？怎样才能让他们按照礼品清单送礼？现在几乎收不到任何东西。’虽然打破传统习俗在我看来总体上是件好事，但婚礼中出现的这种带有交易意味的现象，却是一个意想不到的结果。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Maybe unsurprisingly, every person I spoke with felt differently about what to gift, when to present it, and how much to spend. However, there seemed to be a few general rules of thumb that would be helpful to follow. Fagan said couples getting married should stay "conscientious about what they're asking of people" and consider how expensive weddings are to attend, especially if a guest is in their bridal party or attending other weddings that year. "You have every right to ask for everything you want, but your guests also have a right to say no," she said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 不出所料，我采访过的每一个人对该送什么礼、什么时候送以及花费多少都有不同看法。不过，仍有一些普遍适用可供遵循的原则。费根提醒，即将结婚的新人应该“清楚意识到自己对宾客提出的要求”，要考虑到参加婚礼本身就是一笔不小的开销，特别是当宾客身兼伴郎伴娘或是当年还要出席其他婚礼时。她指出：“你当然可以畅所欲言，表达自己的期望，但宾客也完全有权婉拒。”

paragraphs.contentEn: For wedding guests, give what you can and don't worry about following popular societal rules, like matching the cost of your food at a wedding. "Your $150 is not covering your plate, just in terms of what weddings cost in any high-cost-of-living city, which I think is most cities these days," Ladouceur said. Fagan added: "For every aspect of wedding attendance, you need to be very candid about what you can and can't do, and not feel guilty for setting reasonable boundaries around your finances."
paragraphs.contentZh: 对于参加婚礼的宾客而言，明智的做法是量入为出，不需要被“礼金必须覆盖餐费”这类盛行的社会惯例所束缚。拉杜瑟表示：“你的150美元根本不足以支付婚宴成本——特别是在生活成本高昂的城市，而如今大多数城市的生活成本都很高。”费根补充道：“在婚礼的每一个环节，你都需要坦诚面对自己能做和不能做的事，也不要因为给自己的财务设定了合理界限而感到内疚。”

paragraphs.contentEn: If you're traveling to attend a wedding, she said it's sufficient to hand-make a gift or simply give a card — so long as your care and efforts are clear. What couples ultimately want, Ladouceur said, is "to know you're excited for them." "It's less that people remember what gift you gave, and more that they remember how you showed up for them," she added.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果你即将出席婚礼，费根建议，亲手制作一份礼物，或哪怕只送一张贺卡，都已经足够——关键在于你的心意和真诚付出。拉杜瑟指出，新人们真正渴望的，是“感受到你由衷为他们感到高兴”。她补充道：“多年后人们真正记住的，往往不是你送了什么礼物，而是你如何出席婚礼，如何表达你的支持与祝福。”
